title: Publication Readiness Assessment
description: Evaluation of a research project's scientific quality and suitability for publication in a high-impact journal or conference.

novelty.description: Degree to which the proposed research introduces genuinely new scientific ideas, methods, theories, or findings compared with existing literature. A high score requires substantial, evidence-supported differentiation from the closest prior work. A low score indicates incremental contributions or substantial overlap with existing work.

scientific_significance.description: Importance of the research problem and the potential impact of its contributions on the scientific community. A high score indicates that the research addresses a substantial problem and could meaningfully advance understanding or practice beyond a narrow application.

technical_soundness.description: Correctness and rigor of the proposed methodology, mathematical formulations, algorithms, and underlying assumptions. A high score requires well-justified methodological choices, logically consistent formulations, and the absence of major technical flaws.

experimental_rigor.description: Quality of the experimental design and its ability to substantiate the research claims. Consider dataset selection, meaningful baselines, ablations, statistical validity, robustness, and generalizability. A high score requires comprehensive experiments that convincingly support the claimed contributions.

contribution_clarity.description: Clarity, specificity, and coherence of the research contributions and their relationship to the research questions, methodology, and experimental evidence. A high score indicates that contributions are precisely formulated, distinguishable from prior work, and supported by a coherent scientific argument.

reproducibility.description: Extent to which independent researchers could reproduce the proposed methodology and experimental results. Consider documentation, implementation details, datasets, hyperparameters, random seeds, and accessibility of code or artifacts. A high score indicates that the work is thoroughly specified and practically reproducible.

evidence_maturity.description: Extent to which the claimed contributions are substantiated by completed theoretical analysis, experiments, and validated results rather than planned or preliminary work. A high score indicates that the primary scientific claims are supported by sufficiently complete and reliable evidence.

community_fit.description: Relevance of the research problem, methodology, and contributions to the intended scientific community and its publication expectations. A high score indicates strong alignment with the research interests and standards of a clearly identifiable community. When a specific venue is provided, evaluate fit relative to that venue.

overall_readiness.description: Holistic assessment of the project's current readiness for publication in a high-impact scientific journal or competitive conference. Consider all evaluation dimensions, giving particular weight to novelty, significance, technical soundness, and experimental evidence. Do not calculate this score as a simple arithmetic average.

assessment_summary.description: Concise, critical justification of the overall assessment. Identify the main scientific strengths, most significant weaknesses, likely publication obstacles, and highest-priority improvements. Distinguish established findings from unverified assumptions.
